exposure: Previous obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) severity (3A/3B)
Ongoing pelvic floor symptomatology (bladder pain, difficulties with voiding, sexual dysfunction, bowel dysfunction)
Attendance at a perineal trauma clinic postpartum
cohort: The study included 63 pregnant women with a previous obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) who were attending their first antenatal appointment.
finding: Pregnant women with ongoing urinary symptoms (like bladder pain) were more likely to request a planned Caesarean section, regardless of the severity of their previous tear.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with ongoing urinary symptoms favoured a planned Caesarean section as their preferred mode of delivery.
cross-section timing: During their first antenatal appointment of the current pregnancy
